general_information.Description: The course provides a framework for interpretation, analysis and evaluation of financial statements from viewpoints of creditors, owners, investment firms and others. Thereby, the users of accounting information understand business strengths or weakness, the impact of general business and specific industry situations, behavior of financial markets, credit or lending criteria, and equity investment standards on present and future company financial conditions. After completing the course, the student shall be able to: - Be familiar with the organization and disclosure of reported information - Quantitatively and qualitatively evaluate core accounting issues that are particularly relevant in the context of financial statement analysis. - Have a framework for forecasting future earnings and financial performance. - Evaluate the business financial performance by applying quantitative and qualitative techniques. - Use financial statement information in a modeling environment to identify and recommend solutions to a variety of financial challenges, and to recommend investment decisions.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by the instructor after class - Use laptop in class only for learning purposes - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material on the course, for online support from teachers and other students, and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Apply established techniques, including appropriate technology for analyzing financial statement information for forecasting, valuation, and risk analysis purposes
Integrate and apply the major concepts and theories of fundamental analysis and key steps involved in conducting a fundamental analysis and valuation of a company
Evaluate the impact of financial reporting choices on the quality of accounting information including reported earnings; and assess the quality of accounting information in financial statements.
Use financial statement information in a modeling environment to identify and recommend solutions to a variety of financial challenges
Analyse and synthesise a firm’s financial statement information in the context of the firm’s economic and business condition to make informed recommendations on investment decisions about the firm
Show self-reliance when working independently and collaboratively
Demonstrate ethical awareness and reflection in business context

assessments.Question Type: Exercises, Discussion questions and Constructive questions
assessments.No Question: Depending on the time and schedule of each session.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All chapters and learning materials covered in each session.
assessments.Grading Guide: Participation grades will be given based on students' preparation, quantity as well as quality of participation in the classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and building upon others’ comments.

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7
assessments.Question Type: Group problem solving: 15% for group and 15% for individual. Suggestion: Examine and discuss the financial position of 2 entities in the same industry using their financial statements based on a specific investor/ party's view.
assessments.No Question: Problem solving of a comprehensive business event under a 1,500-2,000 word - report
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Thinking creatively, making decisions, solving problems, Personal qualities: Individual responsibility, self-esteem, sociability, self-management, and integrity.
assessments.Note: Students are free to choose the business cases in domestic or abroad.

assessments.Question Type: Problem solving Suggestion 1: Using knowledge so far, introduce an outstanding finance fraud in business and analyze its effect on the financial statements. Suggestion 2: Pick up an article that mentions about the financial situation of any business, figure out the problem and suggest relevant solutions if needed. Suggestion 3: Case study: analyze problems related to practical problems in financial statement analysis
assessments.No Question: Each part includes 1-2 separate problems/ cases
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: All chapters and learning materials covered from Chapter 1 - 9
assessments.Note: Students are free to choose the business cases in domestic or abroad or assigned by instructors.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Integration of studied knowledge and skills of chapter 1 and 2
